articles.body:
Rockstar is gearing up for the launch of GTA 6, but, of course, Grand Theft Auto isn’t the only series the developer is known for. Alongside the likes of the beloved Red Dead Redemption games, there are many fans of another open-world adventure from the studio: Bully.

Released in 2006 and originally known in Europe as Canis Canem Edit, Bully tells the story of unruly student Jimmy Hopkins getting in and out of trouble during a year at Bullworth Academy. A smaller-scale, less X-rated version of GTA, it launched to critical acclaim. But the road towards launch was far from easy.

“The development was hard,” former Rockstar VP and writer of Bully, Dan Houser, said in a new interview as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “The game was in trouble all of the time. It was difficult. It was an out-there concept. We were struggling with it. I wasn't sure it was going to be any good. We really wanted it to come together. It was really fun afterwards because it came together really well. The team did a great job. It was a sort of really strong game at the end. It kind of came together very late.”

Houser went on to explain why the development of Bully proved such a challenge, coming as it did just over a year after GTA: San Andreas. “New IP is very stressful because you're doing something that no one's ever done before,” he said. “And particularly that game, there was all of this controversy around it to do with the name, or people misunderstood it when they'd never seen it. So I think one of the challenges with that game was it never got the attention it deserved. We were too focused on trying to at least get people to stock it or to not protest it before it even came out.”

The mid-2000s was an era when controversy followed Rockstar games whenever one was about to hit store shelves, whether it be the snuff-film-fuelled ultraviolence of Manhunt, or the sex minigame mod, Hot Coffee, uncovered in the code of San Andreas. Bully was no different, with some members of the public worried about how its explicit content would translate into a school setting.

“There was huge hysteria around it,” Houser stated. “We had to spend most of 2006 diffusing it, so we couldn't positively promote the game in the way we normally would've done. I think that didn't help it. I mean, that was the same time as Hot Coffee, and it felt like things were imploding. It was very stressful. And just go to work each day, wonder who's protesting you that day, and hope that things can shake out properly. I wasn't directly involved. Luckily, I was just sort of right off to the side, and wasn't directly involved in organizing most of that stuff. But it was really stressful for the people involved.”

But it wasn’t just external pressures that made the development of Bully difficult. Rockstar also had to wrestle with how to make its style of open-world action-adventure work from the perspective of a teenager. The school setting meant driving cars and shooting guns had to be parked to one side — two vital gameplay mechanics of any GTA.

“Developers were struggling with what the IP was, and we'd made some changes, and some people had moved out there from New York, and it was starting to get a bit better, but it was still really struggling,” revealed Houser. “It was really, well, if you take away the cars and you take away the guns, what is the game? What are you doing? And the lead designer, who was really talented, began to put in the schedule and began to put in the lessons, and it was starting to get there.

“Then, one of the designers put this thing where you could stick a Post-it note on the back of a character that said ‘Kick me’ on it. Then an NPC would run up and kick them. And just seeing that work, you're like, that's a great moment. So then you're, okay, we're starting to get somewhere. So I think that moment was probably when I always remember going, this IP that wouldn't work in a GTA, obviously; it's not interesting. But as a kid, and suddenly it was the scale of the school and the scale of a kid's life, it started to feel really fun.”

Bully was indeed very fun. So much so that fans have been begging for a sequel ever since. While ideas for a follow-up were once floated around at Rockstar, Houser revealed to IGN in 2025 that it never got off the ground due to “bandwidth issues.”

I do miss the days when you’d get a new Rockstar open world to roam around in every year, but I guess at some point I have to give up yearning for the PS2 era. It was 20 years ago, after all. Luckily, Grand Theft Auto 6 is only weeks away from release.

Simon Cardy is a Senior Editor at IGN who can mainly be found skulking around open world games, indulging in Korean cinema, or despairing at the state of Tottenham Hotspur and the New York Jets. Follow him on Bluesky at @cardy.bsky.social .

articles.title: ‘I Got That Completely Wrong’ — Dan Houser Considers Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 a Failure
articles.summary: ‘I got that completely wrong’ — Dan Houser explains why he thinks Rockstar’s Max Payne 3 ‘failed’.
articles.body:
Max Payne and its sequel, Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne, are two of the most genre-defining third-person shooters ever made. They propelled Finnish developer Remedy Entertainment into the spotlight as one of the most exciting studios making games. So, it was also going to be a challenge for another developer to pick up the third part of that trilogy. If you have the likes of Grand Theft Auto and Red Dead Redemption under your belt, though, you might just fancy your chances.

That’s what former Rockstar VP and writer of Max Payne 3, Dan Houser, thought, and while enjoying the process of making it, he now admits that it didn’t quite hit the mark. Despite being well-received critically, the 2012 game underperformed commercially, and wasn’t a huge hit with players. While Max Payne 3 is a great shooter in its own right, some questioned whether it tonally fit with its heavily noir-influenced predecessors, instead trading in the gloomy, introspective weirdness of Remedy’s New York set games for a more high-octane, colourful, all-action approach.

“It was a linear game, so it was a little different from writing an open-world game, a little more structured,” Houser told IGN as part of our IGN30 Icons Series. “I really enjoyed that as an experience. I loved what we did design-wise, the way the game didn't have loads, the way it felt like a 12-hour movie, some of the visual stuff we did with words on screen. I felt we were creating a really cool digital noir experience, and the consensus at the time was that people hated it.

“So I got that completely wrong,” Houser admitted. “I know Sam Lake [creator of Max Payne] well, and he's a very good guy and really talented. I thought we'd done a good job of doing another Max Payne game. Some people liked it; lots didn't. So we got it wrong, or I got it wrong. I failed. My bit was not a success. The game is beautifully made, and it wasn't as successful as it should have been. So I would say a large amount of that failure was on me as one of the people making the decisions and also as the writer, when people really missed his writing.”

Max Payne 3 is certainly different in tone to what came before it, but I still hold a lot of love for it. Max Payne 2 remains one of my favourite games to this day due to the storytelling housed in its murky world, but there’s no denying that Rockstar brought something new and flashy to the table almost a decade later when taking the character to Brazil.

That bullet time still feels as sweet as ever to trigger, though, and if that level of polish can be brought over to Remedy’s upcoming remakes of the first two in the trilogy, then they can’t come soon enough. We last heard about the project over a year ago, when the studio revealed that it was in “full production” and that the "collaboration with Rockstar Games remains close and productive."

Of course, Rockstar currently has its plate very much full with the imminent launch of GTA 6 on November 19. For more on GTA 6, you can read our full interview with Rockstar co-studio head Rob Nelson , how the game will tackle the current political climate , and why Dan Houser says he won’t be playing it .

articles.title: Dan Houser Was Surprised ‘How Angry Some People Were’ At Red Dead Redemption’s Iconic Ending
articles.summary: Dan Houser was surprised ‘how angry some people were’ at Red Dead Redemption’s iconic ending, and reveals how the decision was made.
articles.body:
Spoilers for Red Dead Redemption and Red Dead Redemption 2 follow.

The ending of 2010’s Red Dead Redemption is an all-timer. For dozens of hours, we’re placed in control of protagonist, John Marston, as he wanders across the American West in search of revenge against his former gang leader, Dutch Van der Linde. He, of course, gets it in a snowy showdown in one of its final missions. But John doesn’t get to live out his life in peace. That would be far too tidy an ending. Instead, the outlaw is gunned down by members of the army at his family farm’s barn.

It was a novel twist at the time. Open-world games, and games in general, didn’t do this. It initially split opinion, but has since gone down as a masterstroke in narrative design. Dan Houser, former VP of Rockstar and writer of Red Dead Redemption, recently spoke with IGN as part of our IGN30 Icons Series, and told us that it was just as difficult a decision to make as it sounds.

“I remember discussing it with the lead designer, Christian Cantamessa, and he was into it, and I was into it, but just knowing the production realities of… how does an open-world game work if you've killed the protagonist? So I said, ‘I think maybe we have to kill him.’ And he goes, ‘That's a great idea. Got to do it.’ I said, ‘I don't know if... let me just think about this,’ because we're just dealing with audio and dialogue. The nature of an open-world game is you finish a story, then you go back into the world and wrap up all the side content if you want to. We'd have to play as someone else for that. We could play as Jack, but what does that mean? So I had to think through for a while what it would mean production-wise.”

Jack is John’s son, and is only 16 years old for the majority of Red Dead Redemption’s runtime. For that transition of control to work, and for the game’s world to make sense, he’d need to become an adult, hence the three-year time jump to 1914 that sees us play as a 19-year-old Jack after his father’s death. But that was just one of the hurdles that faced Houser, Cantamessa, and the team at Rockstar.

“Did we have the skills and the bandwidth to play as Jack?” Houser recalled questioning. “Would it work? Technically, not story-wise. We'll figure out the story aspect. If you go and see a side character and they've got a three-mission arc and you've already done one mission, what would that actually mean if you came back? How would that work? We had to think through all of that stuff and concluded we could probably make it work, but we were still scared.”

The final story mission of the 2010 masterpiece sees Jack carry out his own act of cathartic revenge when he kills the person responsible for John’s murder in a duel. It’s the moment that makes it all work and ties the knot on the game’s story.

“I think people really loved that moment when you killed them and found it so powerful internally,” Houser said. “I think there was broad consensus that it was the right decision, but obviously it was an unusual and out-there decision, but I think the company had survived on making those decisions. I think we were surprised when the game came out by how angry some people were about that decision. There were people who were livid with you. And part of you goes, ‘That's fantastic,’ because it means you've really engaged in the story and the characters.

Another part was like, you forget, or I can forget sometimes, we're not making movies, we're not writing books, we're making games. The game can't live without a player. So they do feel ownership over what you and they are co-creating in the moment in a way someone looking at a painting, say, doesn't. And I think they felt really let down by this decision.

“Now, I think it was the right decision because you want those big, strong reactions, but I think people were really confused by it. As a writer, it was like he had to die for the story to have any weight, and I had wanted that in several GTAs. We’d never done it really for the technical reasons we just discussed.”

Houser seemingly enjoyed it so much that a similar trick was pulled in its sequel, Red Dead Redemption 2, this time arguably to even greater effect as the prequel bound us to Arthur Morgan before Marston once again took over the reins.

In a post-RDR2 world, Rockstar will once again be looking to push its storytelling capabilities forward in GTA 6 by letting us play as a couple on the run, Jason and Lucia. Will we still be able to play as both of them by the time the credits roll?

articles.summary: Pre-order the Pokémon TCG Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box for $119.99 at Walmart, nearly $20 less than Amazon and below TCGplayer market price.
articles.body:
The first wave of Pokémon TCG Delta Reign preorders didn't leave collectors with much choice when it came to prices, but that's already starting to change with a new low retailer price on its ETB.

The lowest price for Delta Reign’s Elite Trainer Box at Amazon right now is $139.94 , through third-party seller Collectors Expedition. However, Walmart has just undercut that just-shy-of-$140 price by nearly $20.

Pokémon TCG: Mega Evolution Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box ETB

Speaking of the trading card marketplace, Walmart’s new low price beats any suitable listings there as well — with the lowest being $122.04 at the time of writing . That said, keep in mind that delivery for the Walmart ETB is currently set for 19 November — 13 days after the Delta Reign expansion hits the Pokémon TCG as a whole.

Whichever site you choose to buy your new Delta Reign Elite Trainer Box from, though, the contents will be exactly the same: nine titular Pokémon Trading Card Game Booster packs, a full-art foil Kyogre promo card, 65 card sleeves, Energy cards, dice, a player's guide, and other usual ETB accessories. Without counting those extras, that works out to around $14.44 per booster pack.

Since the current market price for single Delta Reign booster packs sits at $14.01 on TCGplayer , an extra 43 cents each is a pretty good deal for all those bonuses you’re getting.

As for the expansion itself, Delta Reign is bringing over 135 cards to the Pokémon TCG, headlined by Mega Rayquaza ex, with extra Mega Evolutions like Mega Golurk ex, Mega Malamar ex, and Mega Golisopod ex are also joining the collection, alongside more than 35 Pokémon and Trainer cards featuring special illustrations.

articles.title: The Odyssey Is Up for Preorder, Including a $300 Collector’s Edition
articles.summary: Preorders are live for Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey, including a limited-edition steelbook edition, as well as a $300 collector's giftset.
articles.body:
Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is now available for preorder on 4K UHD Blu-ray at Amazon. It’s set to release November 17, and is available in a number of editions. For starters, there’s a limited-edition 4K steelbook version for $39.99 and a premium giftset for $299.99. Those who prefer standard editions without extra stuff can pick up the 4K standard edition for $29.99 or the DVD for $19.99. Read on for details about what comes in each edition.

The Odyssey - Limited-Edition Premium Giftset (4K UHD)

You can grab the one you want from the list above, or read on for details about what comes in each edition.

The Odyssey - Limited-Edition 4K Premium Giftset

The limited-edition premium giftset also comes with the movie on the movie on 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and digital. It also includes the bonus disc with "an exclusive look at the making of the film." The included steelbook case features a cover that's exclusive to this edition. Here's a rundown of everything included:

If you don't care about having a steelbook case, you can get the movie in 4K for $10 cheaper. This edition also includes the bonus disc with behind-the-scenes features.

The Blu-ray edition also includes a digital copy so you don't even need to put the disc in. It, too, includes a bonus disc with a making-of feature for the movie.

If you're still rocking a DVD player, you don't have to miss out on the ancient Greek action. You can get the movie on that format for $19.99. This edition also includes the bonus disc.

The Odyssey - Limited-Edition 4K Steelbook (Currently Unavailable)

The limited-edition steelbook edition includes the movie on 4K UHD, Blu-ray, and digital. It comes with a bonus disc featuring a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the film.

The Odyssey hit theaters back in July to rave reviews (with the exception of the translator of the epic poem’s most popular edition) and wild success, far surpassing $1 billion at the international box office. It stars Matt Damon, Anne Hathaway, Tom Holland, and more ancient Greeks.

Like Homer’s source material, it’s a largely episodic story as hero Odysseus encounters all sorts of problems as he makes his way back home to Ithaca, where his wife Penelope and his son Telemachus wait. Along the way he encounters a Cyclops, some Sirens, a witch named Circe, and other side quests.

In our review of the movie, critic Scott Collura wrote, “Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey is a must-watch cinematic experience, an epic film version of an epic poem that adapts many of the out-there concepts of Homer through a new eye that frequently brings a sense of horror and existential angst to the story – and even a bit of humor too!”

articles.title: DLSS 5 gets toned down for its Hogwarts Legacy debut next month
articles.summary: DLSS 5 debuts in Hogwarts Legacy and Where Winds Meet next month.
articles.body: When Nvidia originally showed off DLSS 5 earlier this year, the technology immediately got branded as gen AI for video games. To gamers, Nvidia had lost the plot. I personally couldn’t get over how faces were transformed using DLSS 5. The 15-year-old student from Hogwarts Legacy suddenly looked much older, and Grace from Resident Evil Requiem looked yassified. Now more than six months later, DLSS 5 is about to debut properly in Hogwarts Legacy, and it looks like it has been seriously toned down. Nvidia published new comparison screenshots today, where the changes to faces are as subtle as they are in NBA 2K27. Teenagers no longer look like middle-aged men, and even the environmental changes look more subtle. [Image: [Image: Nvidia’s DLSS 5 in Hogwarts Legacy in March. [Image: [Image: Nvidia’s new Hogwarts Legacy DLSS 5 comparisons. Nvidia has always maintained that developers have “detailed artistic control” over DLSS 5, and ultimately make the choice on how to implement the technology in their own games. DLSS 5 will now appear in Hogwarts Legacy on November 5th, and it’s also coming to Where Winds Meet late next month. Nvidia is also improving the performance hit of DLSS 5 with an October update to the neural rendering system that should make it twice as fast on RTX 50-series GPUs and the upcoming RTX Spark laptops. “The DLSS 5 October update shrinks the footprint by 24 percent to roughly 118 million parameters while reducing 4K VRAM usage by 20 percent,” says Nvidia’s Andrew Burnes. This new DLSS 5 model will debut first in NBA 2K27 on October 16th and “will ship by default with future DLSS 5 games.” Alongside the DLSS 5 updates, Nvidia has also shipped a new Nvidia app beta update that includes a faster performance mode for Frame Generation on RTX 40- and 50-series GPUs. The updated AI model uses a “faster and lighter algorithm to boost frame rates” for Frame Gen, Multi Frame Gen, and Dynamic Multi Frame Gen. Nvidia says it has “minor trade-offs in image quality,” and that performance mode for Frame Generation should now be up to 35 precent faster.

articles.title: AI Couldn’t Have Made Star Wars: Galactic Racer’s Biddy Blas
articles.summary: Epic's upcoming Star Wars shooter is reportedly developed with an "AI first" production model, which means it'll never have its own Biddy Blas, Galactic Racer's breakout Weird Little Guy.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Mat Jones. He loves weird little guys in video games.

If your social feed is anything like mine, it’s been overtaken by a weird little crocodile man that’s knee-high to a Tauntaun and has an unresolved rage twelve times his size. His name is Biddy Blas , he’s one of Galactic Racer’s supporting cast, and he’s the best new thing to happen to Star Wars since Andor.

Give an AI as long a time as it needs: it couldn’t have made Biddy Blas.

With every new day, the ground underneath video games as a medium, one where professional creatives are valued and capable of negotiating an honest living, feels more and more unstable. Perfectly good studios are shutting in the name of brand restructuring. Electronic component prices have no incentive to reduce . The cost of producing anything is rising due to the precarious supply of energy and the push to end physical ownership . It’s hard to imagine what the future of the medium looks like, regardless of AI’s role to play in it.

But look, I’m not a doomer – games continue to exist in spite of these truths because of the passion of the people involved. They’re also often better than they’ve ever been. Star Wars: Galactic Racer is a highlight for the under-served genre of arcadey high speed racer, with surprisingly in-depth vehicle customisation, heat management and opponent rivalry systems.

It’s hard not to think about how good it is in the context of Epic Games’ apparent push for an "AI first" production model . Such a pivot has reportedly delayed a secret Star Wars and Marvel crossover shooter, which will apparently be developed with AI tools on both the coding and art sides of the project.

I can’t speak to the quality of a supposed game that is an indefinite time away from release, especially one that no one outside of the Epic offices has seen a frame of, but I can’t see this approach being able to emulate Galactic Racer’s secret weapon. For all the arguments of efficiency, accuracy, and speed, I don’t think a Large Language Model has the capability to create a breakout character. AI cannot make a Biddy Blas.

Blas is an icon. He’s the perfect example of what Star Wars fans have dubbed a “Glub Shitto”; not important enough to the narrative to be a main character, but so arresting in their limited screen time that they become your favorite anyway.

At this point you may be thinking, “Surely a bit of computer code could come up with an angry crocodile in a hat?” And maybe it could. Arguably the main thing that makes Blas so perfect is his ridiculous voice, and AI companies have gone to great lengths to ensure its products can do voices. But, as The Blood of Dawnwalker’s lead actor Will de Renzy-Martin put it on a recent episode of My Perfect Console , “the least interesting thing about what I do is the way my voice sounds”.

"[AI]’s not replicating my personality and the things that I do when I'm in the room, and the choices that I make, which is all the reasons that a director or a producer would want to work with me” said the actor behind Dawnwalker’s protagonist, Coen. "Actors are pretty cheap in the grand scheme of things. And if you end up with an AI that can produce the right noises, you're going to need somebody who can interact with it and get the performance that you want attached to those noises – and they're going to be much more expensive than an actor is."

To put it another way: an AI might have been able to write a nonsense Huttese catchphrase, but only Galactic Racer’s specific writers could have decided one of those sounds was “Scrib Doon”, and only Biddy Blas’ performer, Richard Summers-Calvert, could make the inspired decision to deliver the line as ridiculously as he did. And it’s that combination of creative human decisions, that living understanding of what’s genuinely funny, that turned Biddy Blas from a collection of script and polygons into an icon.

No one can prove a counter-factual, sure; I don’t see the same outpouring of love happening if we outsourced seemingly small decisions like these to the computer. As an anecdote, there’s no reality where my partner would be interested in having a Star Wars racing game hogging the home telly; the Biddy Blas game is an entirely different proposition.

Maybe Epic’s new production pipeline makes sense for a company that has spent the past decade turning Fortnite into a platform more than a game, one that increasingly eschewed creative flair and originality as a driving force (a much ruder critic would say this has never been the ambition at all). The Fortnite of today is now primarily a hub for other brands to throw their licenses at. If the priority of Epic is to focus on streamlining the production process for cramming in things which already exist, an “AI first” approach might seem obvious. If you’re making a Star Wars and Marvel shooter, there are plenty of reference materials for both of those properties to train an AI on. I would simply argue there weren’t reference materials for either… before they existed.

It’s not just Star Wars that needs Weird Little Guys created by Actual Cool People. Players are picking up Valve’s hybrid MOBA-shooter Deadlock in record numbers following its most recent patch, inspired largely by the exciting amount of creative flair displayed by the new inhabitants of the increasingly graphically-realised cursed New York City. Characters like the Rat King, who has hundreds of individually written and performed dialogue barks naming a different one of his rodent subjects for every time one of his abilities is used, or the Chess-hustler Solomon, whose weapon is a board showing historically important endgames chosen by the design team which change depending on the maximum amount of ammo in his magazine. Without people making deliberate decisions, having completely original character ideas, people would not have the same incentive to log in daily to go 0-8 in lane. (Although I hate being in games with these powerful new characters, so maybe this is actually a bad example.)

I see the continued use of AI in ideation and initial production as an existential issue for the medium that we’ll one day be course-correcting away from in the same way it would have seemed obvious to CEOs to chase the seemingly inevitable draw of live-service, online passes and on-disc DLC. For all of the efficiencies in the process, for all the promise of profitability, I’m not sure how you can actually sell any of this stuff without the unique spark of newness. I’m talking about this from a purely cynical marketing perspective: If I’m just going to get stuff I’ve already seen, it’s stuff I already have.

Mat Jones is a Senior Social Producer for IGN based out of London, UK

articles.title: Rockstar's Multi-Million Dollar Miami Takeover Continues to Expand Ahead of GTA 6 Launch, Despite Protests from Some Officials
articles.summary: Rockstar Games is continuing to ramp up GTA 6's massive marketing with a Vice City blimp, NFL promos, and much more, despite protests from Miami officials.
articles.body:
Rockstar Games is continuing to ramp up GTA 6's massive marketing with a Vice City blimp, NFL promos, and much more, despite protests from some Miami officials.

For the last two months, Rockstar has been setting up marketing for what will likely be one of the biggest, if not the biggest, releases in entertainment history. It kicked things off with a massive gameplay reveal on Netflix , followed by a blitz of merch and add-ons such as an album featuring original music created for GTA 6 . Now, Rockstar is taking over the real world to help spread the word of what's to come on November 19.

Rockstar is currently focusing marketing on the city of Miami. GTA 6 takes place in a fictional version of Miami known as Vice City, so Rockstar is utilizing the city for a lot of its advertising, which has led to friction between city officials. Some are all for it, as they hope it attracts more tourism and generates increased revenue. Others, however, are strongly opposed and have been for weeks.

According to The Miamian, County Commissioner René Garcia has expressed displeasure over the marketing campaign for GTA 6 in Miami, reporting he's "really uncomfortable with this whole thing." Specifically, Garcia doesn't like that the city is collaborating with a "game that's depicting Miami like a crime haven; Miami like a murder capital.”

Garcia and other officials are reportedly attempting to squash negotiations with Rockstar to expand its marketing efforts for GTA 6 in the city, which allegedly include ads at Miami International Airport and a $4 million transformation of Miami Beach. The rollout was expected to begin as soon as October 15, but Miami journalist Joel Franco stated that an unnamed official doubts that deals will be finalized in time.

In September, Rockstar paid just shy of $1 million to install a massive, glowing "Welcome to Vice City" sign on top of the Miami Heat's arena, the Kaseya Center . The arena will also be home to an unprecedented NBA game sponsored by Rockstar Games. On November 18, the Miami Heat will play a regular season game against the Milwaukee Bucks on a Vice City-themed court with never-before-seen jerseys inspired by GTA 6 . The arena will also be selling Vice City merch, with Rockstar and the NBA labeling the event as a "night in Vice City."

articles.title: Epic shifts to ‘AI-accelerated development’ for upcoming Disney game
articles.summary: Epic Games has directed developers working on an upcoming Disney game to use AI tools like Claude for the game’s code and art.
articles.body: Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, which is now delayed from its original March release window, according to a report from Bloomberg. The project’s developers have been given an “AI-first” mandate directing them to use tools like Anthropic’s Claude more to finish the game. According to Bloomberg, one of the game’s directors said in a message to staff, “No more hand-written code.” Staff were also told that all of the game’s art will be “generated with full AI workflows.” In a statement given to Bloomberg, Epic Games spokesperson Jake Jones said the company is “embracing AI-accelerated development.” Epic Games and Disney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The upcoming game is reportedly a shooter featuring characters from Marvel and Star Wars. It’s part of a multiyear collaboration between Epic and Disney, which also invested $1.5 billion in Epic in 2024. Epic already uses AI in Fortnite, which has previously featured Disney characters like an AI Darth Vader. But it sounds like Epic may be aiming to have AI do most of the heavy lifting on its new Disney game. AI game development tools have been popping up from other large companies, like Meta and Google, so Epic isn’t alone here. Epic CEO Tim Sweeney has also pushed for Steam to drop its “made with AI” tag, arguing that “AI will be involved in nearly all future production.” Earlier this year, Epic laid off over 1,000 of its employees, following a “downturn” in engagement on Fortnite since 2025.

articles.title: Moana Live-Action Remake Sets Disney+ Release Date After Disastrous Box Office Run
articles.summary: Disney has officially set a streaming release date for the live-action Moana movie.
articles.body:
Disney has officially set a streaming release date for the live-action Moana movie .

The latest remake hits Disney+ on October 21. The move to streaming comes a relatively standard three months after the movie’s initial release in theaters, though struggles at the box office have prompted reactions from Disney as well as questions about the future of the studio's remake strategy.

Moana’s box office hardships go back to the movie’s opening weekend , when it barely managed to beat out the numbers of a previous Disney disappointment, Snow White .

Moana went on to gross just over $162 million domestically, contributing to a total global haul of $323.6 million. It’s currently the 16th highest-grossing movie of 2026 , with a box office total below previous live-action remakes like Lilo & Stitch, Aladdin, and The Little Mermaid.

Ranking the Best Live-Action Disney Remakes

The numbers (and memes ) were enough to spur reactions from a number of the film’s stakeholders. Maui actor Dwayne Johnson, who reprised his role from the animated film, has been open about his disappointment while admitting, “That’s just the way it goes.”

Disney has also openly acknowledged that Moana “underperformed." Disney president Dana Walden attributed some of that underperformance to the decision to release the live-action remake so soon after Moana 2. The animated sequel did fare much better , nearly tripling the box office total of its live-action cousin.

Unfortunately, the Moana remake also struggled to win over critics. IGN’s own 6/10 Moana review derided the film as a “frame-by-frame retelling of the Disney animated musical that doesn't do enough to justify being made.”

Still, the studio remains confident in the franchise as a whole : “Looking ahead, we expect the live-action Moana to be a strong title on Disney+, building on the success of the original film, which is one of the most streamed movies of all time, and extending the reach of the franchise, which now includes three films, a themed area at EPCOT, and a robust global merchandise business."

As it stands, the Rock himself has mentioned development on Moana 3, but there’s no word on whether Moana will continue getting the live-action treatment. Disney doesn’t seem to be doubting their strategy too much, however, with all eyes now on the studio’s next live-action remake: Tangled .

articles.title: The New Friday the 13th Series Crystal Lake Knows What We Want to See: Some Really Fun and Gory Kills
articles.summary: Review: Crystal Lake works in large part thanks to Linda Cardellini’s turn as Pamela Voorhees, while showrunner Brad Caleb Kane brings a thorough knowledge of the original Friday the 13th movies to the series.
articles.body:
All eight episodes of Crystal Lake debut on Peacock on October 15. This is a mostly spoiler-free review, but if you want to know nothing about the show, best to click out of here .

It’s a tricky thing, telling a prequel story. Not only do fans of the thing being prequelized know the ultimate endpoint of the tale being told, but they also already have preconceived ideas about how the events happened which led to their beloved original. Essentially, the creators of a prequel already have the deck stacked against them before they ever even put pen to paper. Or, in the case of Crystal Lake – the new Friday the 13th prequel series – put knife to throat.

But then again, a prequel can work well when it understands how to color (in blood in this case) within the lines of the larger canon while also developing its own world, one filled with engaging characters, a new story worth getting invested in, and enough twists and turns to keep eyes on the screen (before a few of them are inevitably popped out or pierced). It doesn’t hurt to have a cast led by the always great (and recent Emmy winner) Linda Cardellini, either.

Cardellini stars as Pamela Voorhees, a character who your horror-fan buddy is always so proud to remind you – just in case you forgot – was actually the killer in the first Friday the 13th movie , before her more famous son Jason took over in Part 2 . Originally played by Betsy Palmer, Pamela was driven mad when the boy drowned at the Camp Crystal Lake summer camp due to the negligence of a pair of camp counselors, which eventually led the bereaved mother on a killing spree in that first film… before she faced her own unhappy demise.

That’s been the long and short of Pamela’s story since she debuted in the 1980 film, but now showrunner Brad Caleb Kane (who also is a writer-producer on It: Welcome to Derry ) and Cardellini give us a very different take on Pam. Unlike Palmer’s campy whack-job, Cardellini’s Pam is a fully fleshed-out character whom you actually root for, even as the hows and whys of her landing in Crystal Lake with her young son – yes, Jason is here – are slowly revealed over the course of these eight episodes.

It’s a bit tricky to delve into the ins and outs of this show without giving away the various fun surprises that are in store for those who stick with it, but I will say that I really had to let Episode 1 sink in before I was ready to proceed with the rest of the series. Much of this has to do with the inclusion of the 11-year-old Jason (played by Callum Vinson), who is depicted as just a regular little kid who happens to be physically, well, different from the other kids at camp. Caleb Kane and his production team manage to find a balance between the different looks of Jason that the consistently inconsistent Friday the 13th movie series has given us over the decades. But it’s also a bit off-putting at first to see this little kid just being, well, a regular little kid who says stuff like “Yes, I’m reading this whole thing tonight!” By the time he’s raising his new machete in the air, which is part of the camping kit that Pam ordered from him, well…

But then Cardellini and Vinson get to have some really tender moments together, and you feel bad for wishing Jason was just the mute, mutated, monster from the movies. This is a prequel, after all, and you know we’ll get there eventually! And indeed, Caleb Kane reminds us of this when Jason is soon out of the picture, as cinematic fate has prescribed.

What Crystal Lake is really about, then, is how Pam goes from normal, loving mother to the not-mute, not-mutated, but definite monster that she’ll be when she one day puts an arrow through Kevin Bacon’s throat, among other dastardly acts. The character’s slow descent is methodically traced over the course of this season, as she has to deal not just with the loss of her son but also with her mysterious past which has come back to haunt her… and which she seems more than a match for, physically at least. Jason must’ve gotten his skills with a blade from somewhere!

The show populates its cast of townies and campers with various degrees of effectiveness. Cameron Scoggins as the not-too-smart Officer Dorf – a legacy character from the movies! – is a lot of fun, while Gwendolyn Sundstrom plays Jason’s young, troubled friend Grace. The latter is a character who adds a new layer to what we thought we knew about the Jason origin story; she serves as a sort of Jason stand-in for Pamela after her son is gone, for better and worse. Some of the other townsfolk are less interesting, though, and feel a bit too “supporting TV cast” for their own good.

Still, the most notable of the group beyond Cardellini is William Catlett as Sheriff Levon Brooks, who like Pam has a murky past he’d rather not dredge up, even while he can’t fully shake it. His empathy for Pam leads to a strong relationship between the two, with both actors finding different shades to play therein. How much does Pam really care about Levon, versus how much is she using him to buttress herself against any suspicion regarding the increasing number of violent incidents happening around town? Cardellini never fully lets on.

And about those incidents… Crystal Lake does not hold out when it comes to the bloodletting, kicking off with a fairly insane fight scene in the pilot episode that goes from scary to funny and back again. I didn’t keep count, but just about every episode has some kind of tour de force scene of crazy gore that will have you either gasping or chortling… or both, depending on how you feel about such things.

Caleb Kane and his writers certainly know the source material, and they cleverly write in and around events that will eventually happen in the movies (a rewatch of the original Friday the 13th in particular is worth it for fans, if not required). By the time Crystal Lake nears the end of these eight episodes, some of those same fans may be frustrated by certain developments or tweaks or additions to the overall Jason universe, while others will be gratified by how it’s all come together. But you know what they say: You can’t make a Friday the 13th prequel without killing some horny teens – or annoying a few fans.

articles.title: $150 God of War Laufey Collector Box Revealed, No Game Included
articles.summary: God of War Laufey is the next big game to get a collector box without the game itself.
articles.body:
Following in the footsteps of GTA 6, God of War Laufey is the next big game to get a collector box without the game itself.

Sony has revealed the collector box for God of War Laufey, which costs $150 and includes a nice statue of Faye. Unfortunately it does not include a steelbook with a disc copy of the game, or any copy of the game, physically or digitally. Preorders open today at 10am PT through PlayStation Direct, and stock is limited, Sony warned. You can view a full breakdown of the box's items below.

God of War Laufey Collector Box contents:

Light-Up Faye Statue – An eight-inch tall statue featuring Faye, Phranque, and Rue fighting against Begtse’s soldiers. Phranque will light up when the statue is plugged into a USB power source.

51-Card Oracle Deck – Featuring custom illustrations for each card by the talented Megan Lara, the Oracle Deck is a beautiful representation of your adventure through the Everywhen.

Physical Mini Artbook – Concept art depicting the characters, creatures, and environments of God of War Laufey hand-selected by our talented art team at Santa Monica Studio.

Predictably, a lot of people are drawing comparisons to the game-less GTA 6 collector's box . However, some may be a bit more accepting of the value God of War is offering here. GTA 6's box includes a bunch of Vice City-themed merch, such as a pair of sunglasses, a hat, and a figure of a cartoon gator named Macca. It also costs a whopping $400, which is tough to swallow.

Many were critical of the fact that GTA 6's box didn't include a statue of Jason and Lucia , in addition to feeling like the box could've been cheaper if it didn't include certain items. So, God of War Laufey may not be as egregious to some fans given it is a smaller box with a statue of the protagonist. Still, it does feel a bit lacking compared to previous God of War collector's editions.

God of War Ragnarok's collector's edition included Thor's hammer, a steelbook (no game disc, though), DLC, a code for PS4 and PS5 copies of the game, and a handful of other trinkets. God of War 2018's collector's edition included a statue of Kratos and Atreus, a steelbook with a disc, a physical map, a litograph, and two small figures of Brok and Sindri, in addition to a bunch of digital content.

While this is likely supposed to be an add-on for people who are already planning on buying the game, it's disappointing that God of War Laufey's box doesn't at least include a complimentary upgrade to the game's digital deluxe edition, which includes special armor and weapons in the full game.

God of War Laufey – Collector Box will be available in "highly limited quantities" exclusively direct from PlayStation on February 16, 2027 for a recommended retail price of $149.99 USD/ €149.99/ £129.99. Preorders begin today, October 13, 2026 at 10am local time.
